races.name: Watch Unbridled On attheraces.com Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kom Tu Voudras
runners_data.note: Returned just 8 days ago and has strong sim-going form (6 runs on Good, 1 win 3 places), but this hold-up style requires a genuine gallop over 2m5½f at Fontwell to get competitive, and a lone, controlled front-runner makes that hard to guarantee.
runners_data.comment: Kom Tu Voudras bounced back to winning ways four starts back and has run over today's trip, with a quick eight-day turnaround suggesting she's fit and ready; the fall last time is the one concern connections must put behind them.

runners_data.name: Motazzen
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's eight-year-old has a 0/4 trainer-14-day record and only one place from three sim-going runs, but as the sole confirmed front-runner he controls the tempo; a STYLE_FIT flag notes this is slightly out of role as a lone leader, though the lack of challengers mitigates that concern meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Motazzen won three starts back and returns here in good order on just 12 days' rest, having run over today's trip before and carrying 159 lb off a mark of 105. The worry is that his two most recent efforts have both disappointed.

runners_data.name: Break Point
runners_data.note: Luke Dace's hold-up gelding comes here 37 days fresh and has won over 16f on Standard — the step up to 2m5½f on Good at Fontwell is an untested combination, and the apprentice booking (Freddie Keighley, 5lb) adds a minor navigation risk at a tricky course.
runners_data.comment: Break Point shaped with promise when third two starts back and has the profile of a horse ready to strike after 37 days off, his rating of 108 giving him sound claims at the weights; the worry is he was unplaced three starts back, hinting at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Easter Icon
runners_data.note: Won last time out 23 days ago over 19f on Good going, and Gary Brown's charge boasts two wins from seven sim-going starts — a prominent style means this horse is ideally positioned to shadow Motazzen and pounce if the leader weakens late.
runners_data.comment: Easter Icon has winning form in his last five starts but a brought-down and three poor efforts weigh against him, and he ranks last on our figures here; the 157 lb burden does him no favours either, though he does have experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Baltray
runners_data.note: Emma Lavelle's stayer has placed three times over 26f on Good and stays all day, but is a genuine hold-up type pushed forward on the positional map because the back of the field is crowded; the STYLE_FIT flag and 35-day absence temper expectations unless the race truly develops into a stamina grind.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and winless in his last five, Baltray nonetheless heads the ratings on today's trip and returns after a 35-day break with 156 lb to carry — his profile marks him as the one to beat if that placed effort translates here.

races.paceDynamic: Motazzen is the lone confirmed front-runner in a five-horse field over 2m5½f on Good ground at Fontwell, and with no genuine rival to press him, Brendan Powell can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. Easter Icon is a prominent-type who may track closely, but Motazzen's lead is unlikely to be seriously contested, meaning the pace will be honest rather than searching. Kom Tu Voudras and Break Point are both hold-up horses who will need the race to be truly run to deliver their best from off the pace, while Baltray is a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the field's rear is occupied — its true role is at the back, not tracking midfield. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader on a fair gallop over a staying trip — most favours prominent-to-close types who can sit within striking range and pounce at the final flight, rather than deep hold-up horses who need a stronger tempo to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Motazzen Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Motazzen bowls along at the front unchallenged and the pace proves honest enough to stretch the field without burning him out.
scenarios.body: Motazzen sets the fractions he wants, Easter Icon shadows him in second, and neither is ever truly threatened by the hold-up horses failing to generate late momentum on a fair but not punishing gallop. Prominent-to-front types benefit directly as the back-markers lack the pace injection needed to reel in a measured leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely searching and the leaders empty in the final half-mile, leaving a late finisher to pick up.
scenarios.body: Kom Tu Voudras, with sim-going form and experience at this sort of trip on Good ground, would be best placed of the hold-up brigade if the pace is stronger than anticipated. Break Point is also a possibility but has less convincing credentials at this trip and course type, limiting confidence in either delivering.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Easter Icon Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Easter Icon tracks Motazzen closely, waits for the leader to weaken, and the hold-up horses are left too much to do.
scenarios.body: Easter Icon won last time out on Good going over a similar trip and is well placed stylistically to travel prominently before striking; an apprentice pilot (Isabelle Ryder, 5lb) keeps the weight competitive. If Motazzen fades after leading throughout, Easter Icon is the most natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Baltray Defies The Drift
scenarios.trigger: If the true hold-up horses — Baltray in particular — find themselves in better position than their redistribution suggests and the race truly develops into a test of stamina.
scenarios.body: Baltray has placed three times over 26f on Good and stays well for Emma Lavelle, but the STYLE_FIT flag and redistribution caveat mean this shape requires things to go unusually right in terms of traffic and pace. Ben Jones would need a muddling, stop-start gallop to bring Baltray's stamina into play from an unfavoured position.

watchPoints.text: Motazzen's fractions are the race — watch whether Brendan Powell is allowed to coast in front undisturbed or whether Easter Icon pushes up to apply any pressure at all in the early stages.

Baltray's true hold-up role means Ben Jones may struggle to find the position the map implies; watch whether Baltray settles at the rear rather than midfield, which would leave it needing a significantly stronger pace than anticipated.

Break Point's jumping record and the step up in trip to 2m5½f on Good at the quirky Fontwell track is an untested combination — watch for any fluency issues at the early hurdles that could compromise its position.

Easter Icon's apprentice rider Isabelle Ryder (5lb) faces a tactical challenge tracking a lone leader at Fontwell's figure-of-eight layout — watch how she positions relative to Motazzen from the outset, as that will define the finish.

races.name: Download The At The Races App Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Grey Sands
runners_data.note: Kim Bailey & Mat Nicholls yard has been quiet at 0/3 in the 14-day window; this horse's natural instinct is to close from the rear, but the field's make-up means it will be forced to race closer to midfield than ideal, reducing the scope for a trademark late swoop on good ground.

runners_data.name: Houndswood Willow
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe sends this one over from the flat ranks and its best form has come on good ground; though instinctively a hold-up type, there's a real chance it secures a prominent berth with David Bass aboard given how few horses will actively want to lead, which could play to its stamina strengths.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Mo
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish flag and is ridden by a 7lb claimer, which is a concern in a race where novice jumping errors are likely; a true hold-up operator by nature, it will likely find itself racing in the middle of the pack and needs a cleaner, stronger finish than its form suggests it can produce.

runners_data.name: Nicolai
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's charge has pulled up on its most recent hurdles start and fades late according to its profile tags; a natural hold-up type that has struggled consistently on standard ground, it will need a significant step forward in both jumping and finishing to feature.

runners_data.name: October Surprise
runners_data.note: Sheena West's runner has placed once in 14 days at 1/4, giving a small positive yard signal; has only finished in the frame once in six similar-going runs but has reasonable experience over staying trips and Marc Goldstein's front-foot approach could see it sit more prominently than its hold-up profile suggests.

runners_data.name: Rum Diamond
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in the race, off 151 days and tagged with a fade-in-finish warning — if he finds his jumping rhythm he can control the race entirely, but the fitness question after five months off and the Fontwell climb is a real doubt in the final stages.

runners_data.name: Salkadan
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride for the Dan Skelton yard, which is firing at 8/27 in the 14-day window — that combination demands attention; has a win and two places on good ground over staying trips and, while naturally a hold-up type, the prominent headgear tag and quality of connections suggests he'll be ridden to travel close to the pace.

runners_data.name: Short Symphony
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no last-run date and lightly raced flag; Bryan Carver rides for a small yard with a minimal recent record, so form expectations are impossible to set — treat as a wildcard whose price may overestimate or underestimate its readiness.

races.paceDynamic: Rum Diamond is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner juvenile maiden hurdle at Fontwell over 2m1½f on good ground, and with no rival likely to push hard for the lead, he can control matters from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop. The remainder of the field — Salkadan, Grey Sands, Houndswood Willow, Just Call Me Mo, Nicolai, October Surprise, and the unknown quantity Short Symphony — are all hold-up or midfield types by profile, meaning the early sections are unlikely to be truly searching. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Salkadan (prominent headgear, Dan Skelton yard in form) and Houndswood Willow are the most likely to push forward and grab a prominent position ahead of the genuine closers, but most will be shuffled wider in the field than their natural style demands. A controlled, single-paced gallop set by Rum Diamond with few pressing him suits horses who can travel prominently and produce a clean round of jumping, rewarding the horse who can sit closest to the pace and pounce — a prominent-to-midfield profile with clean hurdling technique is what this race shape is built for.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rum Diamond Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rum Diamond leads from the front with no meaningful pressure and the field strings out behind at a steady pace.
scenarios.body: Rum Diamond dictates on his own terms over the unique Fontwell figure-of-eight circuit, and any horse sitting second or third with clean jumping can cruise into contention off a slow tempo. The prominent-seated runner who travels well and jumps fluently — particularly Salkadan, who has form on good ground and backing from a firing stable — is best placed to reel him in late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Overrun Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the steady gallop compresses the field in the straight and hold-up horses get a clear run to swamp the leader on the climb.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race at Fontwell can see a wall of horses descend on the leader in the final climb to the line, and with so many hold-up types forced to race closer than ideal, a late surge becomes plausible. Salkadan and Grey Sands, both carrying natural hold-up profiles, could benefit if they secure cover and produce a strong finishing burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Rum Diamond fades after a solo lead and the horse who tracked him closest outstays the field up the run-in.
scenarios.body: Rum Diamond is tagged with a fade warning and has been off 151 days, so if he ties up late, the horse who has raced prominently throughout — most likely Salkadan or Houndswood Willow — takes the spoils without needing to find a finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Short Symphony or October Surprise, with unknown or underestimated profiles, finds the pace perfectly suited and delivers an unexpected performance.
scenarios.body: Short Symphony is lightly raced and completely unexposed over hurdles, so a well-judged ride by Bryan Carver around a track that rewards accuracy could produce a shock result. October Surprise has shown enough flat form over a mile-plus to suggest stamina for this trip if the pace is truly honest.

watchPoints.text: Salkadan — Dan Skelton at 8/27 in 14 days with Harry Skelton in the saddle is the sharpest form angle in the race; watch him travel prominently and see whether he can put a race together over hurdles for the first time at a staying trip that suits.

Rum Diamond's fitness after 151 days off is the single biggest variable shaping this race — if he ties up on the final Fontwell climb, the entire complexion changes from a front-runner's race to a scrap among closers.

Short Symphony is completely unknown — no last-run data, lightly raced tag, and a small yard, but juvenile hurdle maiden fields frequently throw up surprises from unexposed horses who find the trip quickly.

With so many hold-up horses unable to get their natural position, watch for scrimmaging out of the back straight as several riders simultaneously try to improve their position — jumping errors mid-race are a heightened risk in this field shape.

Houndswood Willow with David Bass — an experienced jump jockey on a horse that needs a prominent spot it may actually be able to claim here — worth monitoring in the early stages to see if Bass takes it forward rather than settling as form suggests.

races.name: Fontwell Park Family Festival Raceday Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kotari
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead from a genuine hold-up profile; the Gary & Josh Moore runner returns after 84 days off and faces a demanding ask racing well outside his comfort zone, though similar-going form (8/15, 0W1P) is modest and Freddie Mitchell's 3lb claim offers marginal compensation.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Kotari has finished third twice in recent starts and shaped with promise each time, making him a solid each-way threat, though the 84-day absence and a hefty 166 lb in the saddle are the risks to overcome.

runners_data.name: Uncle Remus
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's five-year-old ran just six days ago — that quick turnaround is notable — and his similar-going record (7/10, 1W1P) is the most encouraging in the field; Brendan Powell will likely look to track closely in what is effectively a hold-up horse's race despite the compressed midfield.
runners_data.comment: Third four starts back, Uncle Remus shaped better than his recent pulled-up effort suggests, and our rating of 95 marks him as the one to beat in this field; winless in his last five starts, he must bounce back quickly on just six days' rest.

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton teamed up for a win just three days ago with this four-year-old, which flags the horse as fit and in form; his natural style is to come from off the pace but with so many hold-up types present he may race closer than usual, and his recent 22f win on Good suggests the trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Delgany Second Now arrives on the back of a win last time out, his trainer firing at 27% over the past fortnight, and that combination of form and yard confidence makes him a genuine threat here; the concern is a quick three-day turnaround carrying 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Khalk'eau Spigao
runners_data.note: Chris Gordon's four-year-old wears a hood and has shown nothing better than fifth in five similar-ground starts (0W0P); a true hold-up runner forced into a midfield position he does not naturally occupy, and a 58-day absence adds a further question mark.

runners_data.name: Onehundredneighty
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's six-year-old returns after 100 days off the track, which is the longest absence in the field; his best efforts have come on soft/heavy ground and his similar-going record (2/8, 0W0P) is weak, though a placed effort at 2m5f on soft suggests stamina is not the concern — freshness and fitness are.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 100 days off, Onehundredneighty faces a stiff task here, ranked fifth of seven on our figures; third three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement, but the weight of 153 lb does him no favours.

runners_data.name: North Account
runners_data.note: Flags a finishing tendency to fade, which is a serious concern for a horse already racing out of natural hold-up role and mapped to midfield; five runs on Good ground have produced five placed positions no better than sixth, and Nick Scholfield's yard is 2/11 in the past fortnight without obvious improvement.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in recent starts, North Account returns after 49 days carrying 150 lb, and with several runs still to come before his true level is known, there remains scope for improvement as he steps out again.

runners_data.name: Wise Counsellor
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's four-year-old wears a hood and has failed to threaten in four starts on Good ground (8/13, 0W1P); a 66-day absence and a career-best of only sixth on this going make it hard to identify a winning angle even if Caoilin Quinn rides a positive race from a forced midfield berth.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in recent starts, Wise Counsellor returns after 66 days off carrying 149 lb, and with limited form to go on he remains one open to improvement as connections search for a first success.

races.paceDynamic: Kotari is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this seven-runner field and, despite being a natural hold-up horse redistributed to the front, will almost certainly dictate from the outset given the absence of any genuine front-runner among the other six. With all remaining runners being hold-up or midfield types — Delgany Second Now, Khalk'eau Spigao, Onehundredneighty, North Account, Wise Counsellor, and Uncle Remus all naturally wanting to race off the pace — Kotari's solo lead is set to be uncontested and likely to produce a measured, galloping tempo over 2m3f on good ground at Fontwell's unique figure-of-eight track. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate; of those, Delgany Second Now (Harry Skelton, Dan Skelton, recent winner) and Uncle Remus are most likely to push closer than their natural style suggests, seizing the better positions in a compressed midfield. This race shape strongly favours a horse capable of travelling mid-to-prominently and producing a sustained galloping effort rather than a sharp late burst — those who can track Kotari at close range through Fontwell's undulating turns and pounce turning for home hold the clearest positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kotari Controls, Tracks Win
scenarios.trigger: If Kotari bowls along at a fair but uncontested gallop and the closest tracker has the class to reel him in from two out.
scenarios.body: Kotari sets a sustainable fractions on his own, keeping the field strung out on Fontwell's technical circuit, and a horse sitting second or third through the final loop can wear him down on the run-in without needing a sharp sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Kotari goes too hard too soon racing out of his natural style and ties up before the last, leaving a late finisher to scoop the spoils.
scenarios.body: Kotari, uncomfortable on the lead and without natural front-running instincts, over-races and weakens sharply from two out, opening the door for horses held up towards the rear of the compressed field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace, First Run
scenarios.trigger: If Kotari sets only a crawl and the race turns into a sprint finish from the home turn, rewarding the horse quickest to pick up off a slow tempo.
scenarios.body: A false pace bunches the entire field together and the outcome swings on a sharp jump and immediate response to the whip at the last, conditions that slightly favour lighter weights and fresher legs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Brave
scenarios.trigger: If Kotari, despite racing out of role, takes naturally to the lead and finds enough to hold on as the closers fail to close the gap.
scenarios.body: Racing prominently from the front can suit a horse that simply finds its best form when uncontested, and if the chasing pack is slow to commit Kotari could steal enough first-fence-to-last ground to last home.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Kotari, a natural hold-up horse placed on the lead against his instincts, over-races or jumps poorly in the early stages — any error or resistance to the front role could unsettle the entire race shape immediately.

Uncle Remus ran just six days ago; monitor in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of residual fatigue, as a horse that ties up on the back loop at Fontwell can compromise the whole field behind him.

Delgany Second Now's connections (Dan and Harry Skelton) have been in sharp form (8/27 in 14 days) and the three-day turnaround suggests the horse is very well; watch for an aggressive early move to grab a prominent position that his natural hold-up style would not normally see him seek.

North Account is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and has a career record of 0W0P on Good ground over five attempts — worth monitoring as a race-spoiler if the pace is muddling and he briefly threatens before emptying.

The entire field bar Kotari is composed of hold-up types compressed into a midfield cluster; watch the jumping at the first two hurdles for crowding or interference that could decisively reshuffle positions before the race settles into its shape.

races.name: Back A Winner - Birchwood Kia Chichester Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Youdecide
runners_data.note: Won last time out at Goodwood 21f on Good, beating the drop-back to this trip with solid sim-going stats (2W from 5 on similar ground); natural hold-up style is well-suited if pace is genuine, and Ben Pauling's string is in form (T14: 3/7); 3-day turnaround is tight but connections clearly believe the horse is in peak order.
runners_data.comment: Youdecide returns just three days after scoring last time out, and that recent winning form is the key angle here; he has run over today's trip and carries 175 lb, though the quick turnaround is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on Good ground including a 26f success give it strong course-type credentials; hold-up style matches a race where closers are expected to dominate, and the horse's 10-from-15 sim-going record (4W) is the best in the field; tongue tie added, Harry Reed rides for an in-form yard, and 13-day freshener looks ideal.
runners_data.comment: Edgewell won back-to-back two and three starts back, returns in sharp order just 13 days since his last outing, and has run over today's trip before, making him a serious threat at the weights; the main concern is his sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Pawpaw
runners_data.note: Returns from a 551-day absence which is the dominant concern — even with a tongue tie and a course win on Good ground in its profile, that length of absence almost always requires a run to reach peak fitness; though technically a hold-up type, the redistribution note reflects that it may end up closer than usual in a field saturated with rear-runners, potentially masking its true latent ability.
runners_data.comment: Pawpaw won last time out and has run over today's trip, giving him solid claims here, and his 162 lb burden is a significant impost after a lengthy 551-day absence that must be overcome.

runners_data.name: King Of The Story
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old whose entire sim-going record (15 from 15 runs on Good) shows durability if not dominance (3W4P), and he stays well at 2m+; the hold-up style is his natural game but with the rear of the field congested he will need to negotiate traffic from further forward, which is not his comfort zone — 37 days between runs is a straightforward gap.
runners_data.comment: King Of The Story has experience over today's trip but has pulled up twice in his last three starts, and is winless in recent starts; a second four starts back offers some hope, though the burden of 153 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Helios Allen
runners_data.note: Returns from 726 days off which is an enormous concern regardless of any other factor — even a genuine hold-up horse in peak form would need race fitness after two years, and Helios Allen's last five form figures (9,8,9,6,5) on similar going suggest a horse already below winning level before the layoff; p-headgear suggests the stable knows the horse needs help.
runners_data.comment: Helios Allen rates narrowly clear of these rivals on our figures, and he has run over today's trip before, giving him a solid grounding for the task; the glaring concern, though, is that he is winless in recent starts and returns after a 726-day absence carrying 148 lb.

runners_data.name: Of Corse I Can
runners_data.note: Consistent placer in recent starts (five consecutive 4th or 5th finishes on Good and Soft) but unable to convert; natural hold-up style is authentic but the redistribution to midfield reflects an overcrowded rear in this field, and that slight positional compromise combined with no win since 2020 (implied by form string) makes this look a place contender at best under Bradley Harris's 3lb claim.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of fifth and sixth-place finishes offering little encouragement, Of Corse I Can ranks last on our figures and faces a stiff task under 145 lb, though he has run over today's trip and returns on a reasonable 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Ballinoulart
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, giving him a clear tactical advantage in terms of position; however, his OR of 69, seven-pound claim rider (Richard Upton), and form figures showing no win in recent starts (224325) suggest he is better placed as a pace-setter than a winner — if he controls and is not pressured he could run a big race, but finishing it off is the question.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Ballinoulart makes this a tough pitch — though he has run over today's trip before and a second two starts back shows he retains some ability, even if a win continues to elude him.

races.paceDynamic: Ballinoulart is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner handicap chase over 2m5½f at Fontwell on Good ground, and with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, he sets a solo, controlled tempo from the front. That uncontested pace is genuinely sustainable — Ballinoulart has form figures of 224325 and has been placed prominently before, but without any pressure horse to force a genuine gallop, this race risks becoming a crawl before a sprint off the home turn. The field contains far more hold-up horses than can realistically operate from the rear — Pawpaw, King Of The Story, Helios Allen, and Of Corse I Can are all natural hold-up types who have been redistributed forward on the map simply because the true rear is overcrowded; in practice, several of them will likely track closer than usual, compressing the field into a mid-pace convoy. The dominant tactical verdict is that a controlled, falsely-run contest strongly favours closers and prominent racers with a late gear change rather than deep hold-up runners who need genuine pace to aim at — and the two genuine hold-up horses positioned naturally at the rear, Youdecide and Edgewell, are the profiles most likely to benefit if pace is genuine, but only if the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ballinoulart Controls; Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ballinoulart dictates a modest solo gallop and the field concertinas, horses who can travel smoothly into contention from mid-division profit.
scenarios.body: Ballinoulart sets an uncontested pace that is brisk enough to sort out the field over the fences but not truly punishing, allowing prominent trackers to stalk before striking; Edgewell's strong recent good-ground form (two wins) and proven 2m5f+ stamina make it ideally placed to pounce off this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Messy Scramble; Form Horses Land
scenarios.trigger: If the overcrowded hold-up group forces chaotic early positioning and the pace becomes uneven with surges and checks.
scenarios.body: Several redistributed hold-up types jostling for rear berths creates a ragged, stop-start gallop that suits horses who jump fluently and maintain rhythm; Youdecide's recent Goodwood win on Good and Edgewell's string of placed runs at this trip and going give them the class edge when order is restored.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Ballinoulart Runs Away
scenarios.trigger: If the field allows Ballinoulart to bowl along completely unchallenged at an even hunting pace and the rest fail to organise a challenge.
scenarios.body: A completely uncontested front-runner at a circuit like Fontwell, where the figure-of-eight layout rewards jumping accuracy, can steal a march before rivals realise the pace is slow; Ballinoulart's consistency record (five places from recent runs) and lower weight make this a genuine if minority threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail; Pace Too Slow
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so falsely run that hold-up horses simply cannot reel in a front-runner with momentum over the last two fences.
scenarios.body: A truly crawling pace removes any advantage for hold-up types whose style depends on making ground into a real gallop; Pawpaw (tailed off 551 days absent but a course winner on Good) and King Of The Story, despite style-fit concerns, could grab minor honours if they are forced up close enough to capitalise on the slow tempo.

watchPoints.text: Watch Edgewell's jumping closely — two recent Good-ground wins over 23f-26f make it the most credible challenger to a controlled Ballinoulart tempo, and if it travels smoothly through the Fontwell bends it could hit the front earlier than rivals expect.

Ballinoulart's rider Richard Upton claims 7lb which is one of the deepest claims on the card — watch whether the weight advantage is enough to offset inexperience at controlling a front-running ride on Fontwell's idiosyncratic figure-of-eight circuit.

Pawpaw's 551-day absence is a red flag for punters — watch its behaviour in the parade ring and early jumping for any sign of rustiness before drawing conclusions, as a poorly-jumping or unfit horse returning from that layoff could cause interference at a fence.

Monitor how many of the redistributed hold-up types (King Of The Story, Helios Allen, Of Corse I Can) actually take a position close to Ballinoulart in the early stages — if several drift forward the pace could quicken sooner than expected, changing the complexion of the race entirely.

Youdecide's 3-day turnaround after its last run bears watching in the pre-race — Ben Pauling's T14 figures (3/7) suggest confidence, but a six-year-old running again within 72 hours must show no sign of physical wear before being relied upon to reproduce its winning run.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Camshaft
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner who has won twice on good ground over comparable trips, confirmed by her 1W2P sim-going record; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. in the saddle for a yard in decent recent form (2/19 T14), 44 days fresh, and wearing headgear — looks set to control this from the front unchallenged.|
runners_data.comment: Camshaft arrives on the back of back-to-back wins two and three starts ago, and though third last time out, she remains in cracking nick; carrying a hefty 168 lb after 44 days off is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Mobile Mamma
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners a mare whose best run came when winning over 24f on good ground, but her 11th last time out over the same trip is a concern; a true hold-up type who needs a strong gallop to deliver her best, and Fontwell's circuit does not always provide one.|
runners_data.comment: Mobile Mamma has been knocking on the door, finishing third and then second in her last two starts before an unplaced effort, and 21 days gives her a clean freshening; the concern is that 161 lb is a hefty weight to carry while still seeking that elusive first win.

runners_data.name: Luna Run
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins from 15 runs on similar going including a win at 26f in this exact style of race; Harry Derham's yard has had a runner placed recently (T14: 1/3), and 40 days off gives her a fresh look for this stamina assignment.|
runners_data.comment: Luna Run showed a winner one start back but has been in and out of form otherwise, and ranked sixth of seven on our figures she faces a stiff task under 156 lb, though she does have experience over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: Just three days since her last run which is an immediate stamina-test concern over 3m2f; prominent in style but all her form comes over shorter trips (17-18f), and stepping up significantly in distance for the first time adds a major question mark despite Chad Bament's 5lb claim.|
runners_data.comment: Steal A Glance arrives here just three days after finishing second last time out, and that near-miss is the standout angle for a filly who commands the highest rating in this field; winless in her last five starts, she will need to convert promise into reward under 151 lb.

runners_data.name: Athena's Dream
runners_data.note: A prominent type who has placed at 23f and 24f on good ground and handles this going well enough, but the 7lb claimer Megan Bevan is an inexperienced partnership and the mare's form string (74-235) shows no win yet — needs career-best to be a factor.|

runners_data.name: Lynsey Larue
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday which is an extreme freshness concern and must be treated with significant caution on fitness grounds; her one win came over 24f on soft and her 8/13 sim-going record suggests good ground is merely adequate rather than ideal for this hold-up mare.|
runners_data.comment: Ran just yesterday and already back out carrying 150 lb, which makes her hard to fancy; she was pulled up two starts back, though a winner three starts back and third last time out are the positives in an otherwise testing profile.

runners_data.name: Glorious Mist
runners_data.note: A 96-day absence, poor recent form (pulled up twice in her last four), and an OR of 67 make her a significant outsider; her actual running style is hold-up but the congested field has pushed her map position forward — she races off-role here and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 tempers any confidence in her chance.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts yet her rating of 92 puts her firmly in contention here, and experience over today's trip is a clear asset at 142 lb; the main concern is a troubled recent spell of falls and pull-ups that makes her current wellbeing hard to gauge after 96 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Camshaft is the sole confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she should cruise into a comfortable, uncontested position from the outset over this stamina-sapping 3m2f trip at Fontwell. Luna Run, Steal A Glance, and Athena's Dream are all prominent types who will push forward behind her, creating an organised if somewhat clustered early order rather than a messy pace battle. Mobile Mamma, Lynsey Larue, and Glorious Mist are hold-up types, though Glorious Mist has been redistributed to midfield on the map because this field contains more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Mobile Mamma and Lynsey Larue are most likely to secure the natural off-the-pace positions. With Camshaft setting a fair but manageable gallop on good ground, this race shape strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles that can travel comfortably within striking range and avoid the attrition of having to make up ground on Fontwell's idiosyncratic, tight-turning circuit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Camshaft Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Camshaft dictates a sustainable front-running display and holds on from the front
scenarios.body: Camshaft sets a comfortable tempo unchallenged, conserving energy through the early stages of this stamina test, and her recent course-and-distance-relevant form on good ground gives her every chance of lasting home. Prominent types who have tracked her closely, particularly Luna Run, are best placed to pounce if she tires, but the uncontested lead is a significant advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Camshaft sets too strong a pace for herself and one of the prominent trackers picks her off in the closing stages
scenarios.body: Luna Run or Steal A Glance, tucked in behind on a good surface that suits their recent form profiles, stays close enough to the leader throughout and benefits if Camshaft's gallop proves marginally too keen over this extreme trip. This scenario suits the prominent types who can travel fluently at Fontwell's circuit without expending unnecessary energy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to set up a decisive finish for a closer coming from off the bridle
scenarios.body: Mobile Mamma or Lynsey Larue, held up in arrears by Skelton or Ring respectively, would need a genuinely pressured pace to generate the momentum required to reel in leaders around Fontwell's tight bends — a circuit that notoriously punishes horses who must make up significant ground. Given this field's limited collective pace and Camshaft's likely uncontested front-running, the prospect of a truly strong gallop materialising is modest at best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition And Atypical Result
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners make errors, fall back, or the race deteriorates into a messy, slow-sectioned affair
scenarios.body: Fontwell's technical layout and a long 3m2f trip over hurdles can occasionally produce scattered, untidy races where the least error-prone survivor picks up the pieces. Glorious Mist, though lightly regarded and out of form, has experience over this style of trip in good ground, and a chaotic race shape could theoretically bring her back into contention despite her redistribution and poor recent figures.

watchPoints.text: Steal A Glance ran just three days ago — monitor closely in the paddock and early stages for signs of fatigue over this significantly longer trip than she has attempted before.
Glorious Mist returns from 96 days off with two pulled-up runs in her recent past and is at risk of doing the same again — connections and market moves should be watched before the off.

Lynsey Larue ran yesterday and connections have not explained the decision to run again within 24 hours — her jumping sharpness and early position should be monitored as she could fade quickly in the closing stages.

If Camshaft is allowed a completely uncontested lead by the other prominent types (Luna Run, Steal A Glance), watch whether the pace becomes too steady — a slow gallop over 3m2f could compress the field and bring the hold-up horses Mobile Mamma and Lynsey Larue dangerously close at the finish.

Luna Run's jockey Paul O'Brien should be tracked from the outset — if he pushes up to sit directly behind Camshaft in second, she becomes the most dangerous immediate threat to the front-runner in the final mile.

races.name: Free Tips Daily On attheraces.com Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Person of Interest
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who appreciates a truly-run race to close into, and this pace map sets that up perfectly; Faye Bramley's yard is 1/10 in a 14-day window but Harry Cobden provides a significant jockey upgrade, and two wins from five on similar good ground underlines the surface suitability across the extended trip.
runners_data.comment: Person of Interest showed his class when winning two starts back, and followed up with a second last time out to advertise strong current form; carrying 167 lb after 47 days off is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: She Is For Me Boys
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner who will battle A Little Something for supremacy from the jump; the tongue-tie flag (hg:t) points to a horse who must dictate, and her 4W8P record on good surfaces is solid, but a 60-day absence and a claimer in the saddle raise questions about whether she has enough left when it matters.
runners_data.comment: She Is For Me Boys arrives as the top-rated runner in this field, her recent form reading consistently competitive with a win two starts back and a placed effort last time out, and she has experience over today's trip; the concern is whether 60 days between runs leaves her spot-on for this test.

runners_data.name: Merely A Detail
runners_data.note: A five-year-old who runs from the rear and is lightly raced enough to carry an improvement curve; Jonathan Burke is a strong pilot, last run 35 days ago is fresh without being ring-rusty, and two wins from seven on good ground suggest the surface is no issue — the step up beyond 16f in trip is the one open question given the form string.
runners_data.comment: Merely A Detail brings a win two starts back into this, and while the most recent run was voided she returns after 35 days in decent order, has run over today's trip, and her 164 lb burden is the one watch point.

runners_data.name: Two To Tango
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a remarkable 13 runs from 15 on good ground making him highly reliable in these conditions; Charlie Todd rides and Emma Lavelle's 0/4 in the 14-day window is a mild negative, but a 73-day break and prominent style in a pace-contested race means he must show he's sharp enough from the gate to hold that position.
runners_data.comment: Placed second two starts back and third three starts back, Two To Tango has the profile of a genuine danger here, and our rating of 111 underlines his claims; the main concern is a 73-day absence since his last start.

runners_data.name: A Little Something
runners_data.note: The second front-runner who makes this pace battle inevitable; back-to-back wins leading from the front on good ground underline the suitability of conditions, but an 'F' (fall) in her most recent run and a 'U' before that flag jumping fragility under pressure — if she meets a fence wrong in a speed duel she is a primary exit risk.
runners_data.comment: A Little Something has winning form three and four starts back, but a fall and an unseating in her two most recent outings make her very hard to trust, and our rating has her well held by the field's top performers at the weights.

runners_data.name: Martin's Denuo
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hat-trick winner switching from all-weather to turf jumps for the first time, carrying the lightest weight in the field off a 26-day turnaround; the style is genuinely unknown (U-tagged) which is the key uncertainty, and David Pipe's 1/10 14-day record is not encouraging, but raw ability and fresh legs at minimum weight give him a fringe chance if he settles in a chase context.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Martin's Denuo arrives in fine nick with three wins in his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and 26 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh and ready.

races.paceDynamic: She Is For Me Boys and A Little Something are both confirmed front-runners, and with only six runners in this 2m2f handicap chase at Fontwell, the battle for the lead will be immediate and genuine from the off. Neither handler is likely to concede the rail willingly — She Is For Me Boys has front-running form at this sort of trip on good ground, while A Little Something has won back-to-back races leading throughout and carries tongue-tie that suggests she needs to bowl along. The honest, contested gallop this creates will burn up the front two early and place maximum pressure on their jumping, stretching the field out across Fontwell's unique figure-of-eight configuration. This race shape firmly favours hold-up horses who can relax off the pace, travel fresh into the contest in the latter stages, and pick up rivals who have been at each other's throats from the front — making late-running profiles the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If She Is For Me Boys and A Little Something push each other along from the flag, softening each other up and leaving the back-markers fresh for a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: The genuine front-running battle will drain the leaders heading into the final fences, handing the race to those who tracked off the pace and conserve energy. Hold-up and midfield horses arrive with untapped momentum when the leaders tire, making this the dominant and most likely shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one front runner jumps more fluently than the other early, establishing a rhythm that neuters the pace battle and turns this into a solo lead.
scenarios.body: With a clear lead and jumping fuel in reserve, a lone pace-setter can dictate terms and control the fractions enough to grind out the win at Fontwell. She Is For Me Boys, whose record at this trip and going is strong, is the better candidate if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Player Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is just honest rather than brutal, leaving the prominent traveller Two To Tango close enough to capitalise at the business end.
scenarios.body: Two To Tango travels prominently and has an outstanding record on good ground at this type of trip, and the Lavelle yard's course-and-distance form makes this a live alternative shape. Sitting a length or two off a pace battle rather than being immersed in it would let the horse hit the final fence full of running.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Martin's Denuo, switching from all-weather and a hat-trick hunter fresh to obstacles, adapts quickly and exploits youth and a featherweight to close late.
scenarios.body: At just 156lbs off a hat-trick and with an unbeaten sequence behind him, the David Pipe four-year-old carries the unknowns of a chase novice at a unique track but raw ability could bridge the experience gap if the race falls apart in front. The drop in weight and fresh legs give this raw shape a small but non-trivial chance.

watchPoints.text: Watch A Little Something at the early fences — her recent fall and unseated-rider form flags genuine jumping fragility when pressed hard, and She Is For Me Boys will be at her shoulder from the very first obstacle.
If She Is For Me Boys and A Little Something lock horns through the first circuit, monitor both for errors at the ditch fences where fatigue-induced mistakes become likely in a genuine pace duel.

Martin's Denuo is a complete unknown quantity over fences on turf — watch his jumping at the opening obstacles; a novicey leap or two early would confirm he is not a factor and would allow you to focus on the established performers.

Two To Tango needs to travel prominently from the gate despite a 73-day break — if Charlie Todd is caught flat-footed and the horse is shuffled back into the pack early, the tactical edge that makes him competitive in this scenario evaporates.

Person of Interest carries 167lbs and ran poorly on his most recent start (9th) but two of his last five runs at this distance on good ground produced wins — watch whether Harry Cobden positions him to get a tow into the race from the pace battle rather than being left isolated at the rear.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: God Of Fire
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in this field and should dictate from the off; ran well at this trip on good recently and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. will look to use that positional advantage fully, though a STYLE_FIT score of 0.94 suggests he is stretching into a true lead role rather than his most comfortable prominent berth.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and rates a clear nine pounds above his official mark on our assessment; God Of Fire has run over today's trip and returns on a sharp 13-day turnaround carrying 168 lb, with that fourth last time out the only minor concern.

runners_data.name: Best Night
runners_data.note: David Pipe's five-year-old has solid placed form across multiple runs on good ground at this sort of trip and Rian Corcoran's 5lb claim is a useful pull in the weights; a natural hold-up type who needs something to chase, making a sustainable early pace an ally.
runners_data.comment: Consistent form figures of second and third in recent starts make Best Night a genuine threat here, and she has run over today's trip; the main risk is that she remains winless in her last five outings.

runners_data.name: Aggagio
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer who should slot in just behind God Of Fire and get a smooth passage; Gary and Josh Moore's yard is in form at 2/21 over the past fortnight but the form string of 82773- leaves a mark — needs improvement to figure here.
runners_data.comment: Aggagio is winless in his last five starts yet shaped with promise when third last time out, and he has run over today's trip before; carrying 166 lb on a 28-day break is the chief concern for a gelding our rating marks as the second-strongest in the field.

runners_data.name: Brave Guest
runners_data.note: Marc Goldstein partners this four-year-old who has twice finished second at similar trips on good to soft; a hold-up style means he needs traffic to part and a stern enough pace to bring him into the race, with limited good-ground form (3 runs, 0 wins, 1 placed) a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: Brave Guest arrives here on the back of consecutive second-place finishes two and three starts back, boasts experience over today's trip, and at 166 lb our rating of 104 suggests he holds strong claims against this field; the concern is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Double Power
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes the ride but the form figures of 0-9798 paint a bleak picture and the flagged fade in the finish is a significant negative in a race likely to be run at a measured, non-attritional gallop; the prominent style suits positionally yet his tendency to stop talking late is hard to overlook.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of nine on ratings, Double Power faces a stiff ask under 165 lb, though he returns on a sharp 15-day turnaround and has enough class on an official mark of 96 to warrant respect if the headwinds ease.

runners_data.name: Graffiti
runners_data.note: Megan Bevan's 7lb claim helps this seven-year-old carry 160lbs but his recent form has been at shorter trips on firmer or standard ground — the step up to 2m1½f on turf good is a question mark; the one win in his last five came over 10f so the trip may be stretching him.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second two starts back, Graffiti shows consistent placing form yet remains winless in his last five starts, and 52 days off the track is a fitness query; the 160 lb burden is no help, though he has run over today's trip and our rating of 99 suggests some upside.

runners_data.name: Charlie My Boy
runners_data.note: Useful placed record on good ground with 14 of his last 15 runs on that surface, and James Davies is a capable booking for J.R. Jenkins; however, his true style is hold-up from the rear, and with the field loaded with closers he will be pushed forward into a midfield role that does not play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Charlie My Boy has plenty to prove here; he has run over today's trip and the second last time out is a crumb of comfort, but 160 lb is a hefty burden for a horse without a win to his name.

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: Back just five days after his last run but that race was likely light work and his form string of 342135 shows genuine consistency; won over 18f on good and placed repeatedly — a prominent-racing type who may have the soundest recent profile in this field at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Raffles Nobu is hard to fancy ranked bottom but one on our figures, and a fifth last time out — just five days ago — does little to help his cause; he has run over today's trip and does own a win in his last six starts, but 160 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Harry Gulliver
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good and has finished third in that company, so the form is not without merit; his natural style is late-running from the rear, but with several hold-up types present he has been mapped to midfield — a position that does not suit, and at OR 80 he carries the lightest burden but faces a stiff task conceding form to higher-rated rivals.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Harry Gulliver has finished fifth and eighth in his last two starts, making him hard to fancy here. A third three starts back offers slim encouragement, as does the win four starts back, but he faces a stiff ask from 149 lb.

races.paceDynamic: God Of Fire is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival looking to press him from the off, he should be able to control tempo from the front at a sustainable gallop around Fontwell's tight figure-of-eight circuit. Aggagio, Double Power, and Raffles Nobu are the prominent types likely to track him in the first two or three positions, creating a compact early order with the hold-up brigade — Best Night, Brave Guest, Graffiti — settled further back. The field actually carries more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate cleanly; Charlie My Boy and Harry Gulliver are genuine closers who will be forced to race in a more prominent position than is natural for them, compromising their chance of delivering a late run from the rear. With God Of Fire likely to dictate a controlled, uncontested pace, this race shape most benefits prominent racers who can travel smoothly just behind the leader and time their challenge at the penultimate hurdle — patient front-to-midfield types who handle a good surface are firmly favoured over those who need a true test to bring them into it late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: God Of Fire Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If God Of Fire is allowed to bowl along in front unchallenged and the pace is measured enough to preserve his stamina into the straight.
scenarios.body: God Of Fire sets a steady-to-fair tempo and the prominent trackers — Aggagio and Raffles Nobu — are best placed to mount their challenge as the field turns for home, with the leader potentially lasting into the places.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Aggagio or Raffles Nobu travel strongly enough to throw down a sustained challenge before the last and overhaul a tiring God Of Fire.
scenarios.body: The pace proves just quick enough to pop the leader's stamina in the final half-mile, promoting those who tracked him throughout into winning contention; Raffles Nobu's recent win at this trip makes him a natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough to soften the leaders and create genuine gaps for closers to exploit in the final run-in.
scenarios.body: Best Night, with strong placed form at this distance on good ground, is ideally positioned to finish with purpose if the race is run to suit; Brave Guest would also appreciate a test that brings them into it late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is uneven or God Of Fire is pressured unexpectedly, turning the race into a sprint for home where fortune plays a bigger role.
scenarios.body: A ragged tempo scrambles the typical tactical order and any runner capable of quickening sharply off a steady early pace gets a chance; Graffiti's win on good ground and Charlie My Boy's solid placed record become relevant even if their routes through the race are less predictable.

watchPoints.text: God Of Fire — if he is allowed to coast in front unchallenged, the race becomes his to lose before the final hurdle; watch whether any prominent handler tries to press him early, as any pressure before halfway could dramatically change the race shape.

Raffles Nobu — returned just five days ago and runs again here, so watch the market closely for any sign connections are happy; if he travels sweetly in the early stages his consistency at this trip makes him a genuine shape-winner.

Charlie My Boy and Harry Gulliver — both are true hold-up horses who will be riding a position ahead of their comfort zone; if they end up racing too freely or too close to the pace, their finishing effort in the straight is likely to be compromised.

Best Night — with ten of his last fifteen runs on good ground and a clean placed record across that sample, watch whether Rian Corcoran is able to get a clear passage turning for home, as the hold-up style requires an unobstructed run at the field late.

Double Power — flagged as a runner who fades in the finish; if he travels prominently and begins to capitulate after the last, it may drag the field into a messy finish that opens the door for the closers further back.
